newsitem.title: USA: League files action against Schering-Plough.
newsitem.headline: League files action against Schering-Plough.

text.p: The League of Physicians & Surgeons said it filed a class action suit on Monday in New York state court alleging that Schering-Plough Corp mislabeled a Coppertone tanning product, possibly leading to an increase in skin cancer.

The complaint was filed by Yvonne Archer, executive director of the New York City non-profit doctor-patient advocacy group, on behalf of consumers of the Coppertone Gold Dark Tanning Dry Oil Spray SPF 2 product.

The class action alleges that Schering-Plough and its Schering-Plough HealthCare Inc unit falsely labeled the product, stating that it "screens out the sun's burning rays while allowing you to get a deep, dark, golden tan."

According to the complaint, the label allegedly fails to inform users that SPF 2 "provides only minimal short-term protection and that extended exposure to direct sunlight while using the product will result in substantial risk of melanoma and other forms of skin cancer," the league said.
A league spokeswomen said it would seek damages in the case, but that it could not disclose a specific dollar amount.
No one was immediately available at Schering-Plough to comment on the case.
